lines.text: Chanel wore fake pearls on purpose.
Gabrielle Chanel, called Coco, wore real pearls and imitation pearls together.
She often layered several long necklaces over otherwise simple outfits.
A long necklace was a hallmark of her style, the house says.
The V and A says imitation pearls became a Chanel signature.
From the 1920s, jewelry was central to her design vocabulary.
lines.say: From the nineteen twenties, jewelry was central to her design vocabulary.

lines.text: Her work helped raise the status of costume jewelry in fashion.
She is quoted saying it must remain an ornament and an amusement.
The Met keeps a Chanel necklace with faux pearls from about 1959.

lines.text: The V and A holds an imitation pearl necklace from 1959 too.

post.caption: Coco Chanel wore real pearls and imitation pearls together on purpose, layering long necklaces over simple outfits. The V and A calls imitation pearls a particular Chanel hallmark, and from the 1920s jewelry was central to her designs. Her work helped raise the status of costume jewelry, and she is quoted saying it must remain an ornament and an amusement. The Met and the V and A both keep Chanel necklaces with imitation pearls from about 1959.
